decision: Parent selects unchanged camera transform/offset at existing resets, with FOV derived from current posed camera-space vertices; FOV fixed through orbit, not globally fixed across poses/viewports. This supersedes only the earlier globally-fixed-FOV framing question.

formula.inputs: Existing points, unchanged camera transform, validated current aspect (same .85 fallback if viewport invalid).
formula.depth: For q=inverse(cameraTransform)*point, d=-q.z; require every q.x,q.y,d finite and .1<d<100.
formula.proof: Vertical normalized coordinate is q.y/(d*t), horizontal is q.x/(aspect*d*t); both magnitudes <=1/1.08 for all framing vertices. No camera translation/orientation or clip-plane change is required.
formula.orbit: Keep canonical fitted perspective component FOV unchanged. Existing camera offset/zoom supplies perspective magnification once; do not scale FOV as well. Rotation changes foreshortening and may change clipping/framing; canonical fit is not a full-orbit guarantee.

changes: Both single and pair constructors choose one camera component under the immutable DEBUG HANGTEN_REVIEW_ALL_HAND_PERSPECTIVE flag. Perspective placeholder60deg is an explicitly labeled rendering adaptation until first valid existing reset.

Both existing resets branch before camera assignment: perspective computes/guards fitted FOV and updates component; orthographic statement sequence retained. Existing canonical center/offset, transforms, scale bookkeeping and orbit state reset remain unchanged.

Both orbit methods retain existing transform/zoom calculations and bypass only orthographic component unwrap/scale update in perspective mode. All four prior forced unwrap paths remain reachable only in orthographic branches.

Existing recorder emits sparse hand-camera records only at configuration/reset (plus fit rejection), with actual component presence, FOV or scale, near/far, transform and per-vertex depth range. No body logging, observer, periodic sampler, state write or new runtime resource.
Release and diagnostic-orthographic branches retain existing camera behavior; all source changes are a temporary diagnostic proposal, not a production repair.
runtimeGateIfAuthorized: Do not combine strict suppression with perspective; hands must remain enabled and constructor/make positive. Scrub inherited flags in both fresh processes.
Same built binary, same direct natural workout and actual host/viewport/root/camera layout history; first establish orthographic failure, then perspective comparison only under parent gate.
Exactly one hand camera component of intended type; every exercised reset emits reset-fitted with valid near/far depth and no fit-rejected event. Placeholder configuration is not a successful fit.

Match existing camera transform reset values and host/lifecycle inputs across arms. Actual perspective hand pixels will differ because foreshortening is intentional; board geometry/materials must remain unchanged.
Full whole-image and CPU brackets decide rendered behavior; FOV arithmetic and component metadata cannot establish a repair.
limits: No application, typecheck, build, Simulator run, test or hand geometry change.
Diagnostic placeholder60degrees is explicit and temporary; fitted FOV comes from source vertices, never pixels or anatomical/manufacturer claims.

The two nominal orbit paths are covered by branching, but no gesture validation has been performed; untouched clipping at extreme orbit needs prospective coverage if that behavior becomes part of the task.
Original audit, source excerpts and previous decision context remain unchanged.
